conventions.convention: Robust risk is the outer expectation of the pointwise supremum, defined through nonnegative measurable majorants; graph measurability of a threat correspondence does not assert measurability of that supremum. Perturbation balls are closed.

Gaussian branches assume AC, have finite dimension d ≥ 1 and σ > 0, and use balanced labels. Fixed normalized parameters satisfy ||θ||₂ = √d; this normalization is not imposed on the separate Gaussian-prior experiment.
Linear classifiers assign score zero to +1; the sample-mean procedure requires n ≥ 1.
Coordinate thresholding maps zero to +1. Exact preservation of hypercube coordinates is asserted only for perturbation radius ε < 1.

The Bernoulli parameter lies in the sign hypercube; conditional feature signs match yθ coordinatewise with probability 1/2 + τ. The prior experiment uses a uniform parameter and conditionally independent observations.
The Gaussian lower bound permits n = 0, uses an empty sum equal to zero, quantifies over jointly Borel deterministic learning rules, and takes an outer expectation over parameter and sample.

load_bearing.statement: The pointwise robust loss is sup over x′ ∈ Δ(x) of ℓ(f(x′),y); its robust risk is the infimum of expectations of nonnegative measurable functions dominating that loss.

Assume AC. For d ≥ 1, σ > 0 and G ∼ N_d(0,σ²I_d), P(||G||₂ ≥ σ√d+t) ≤ exp(−t²/(2σ²)) for t ≥ 0, and P(||G||∞ > s) ≤ 2d exp(−s²/(2σ²)) for s ≥ 0. Each unit-vector projection has the stated upper and lower one-sided Gaussian tail bounds. For d ≥ 2, P(||G||∞ ≤ 2σ√(2 log d)) ≥ 1−1/d.

For independent sign variables ξ_i, real coefficients c_i, V = Σc_i² and S = Σc_i(ξ_i−Eξ_i), each one-sided tail at t > 0 is at most exp(−t²/(2V)) when V > 0, and the two-sided tail is at most twice that quantity. When V = 0, including the empty sum, all three tail probabilities are zero.

Assume AC. For d,n ≥ 1, σ > 0, ||θ||₂ = √d and independent Gaussian-model observations, let W = n⁻¹ΣY_iX_i and normalize it, using e₁ when W = 0. Then P(⟨Ŵ,θ⟩ ≤ ((2√n−1)/(2√n+4σ))√d) ≤ 2 exp(−d/(8(σ²+1))).

Assume AC. Under prior Θ ∼ N_d(0,I_d), n ≥ 1 conditionally independent observations Z_i ∼ N_d(Θ,σ²I_d), and independent uniform labels, the posterior is N_d((n/(σ²+n))Z̄,(σ²/(σ²+n))I_d). With n = 0 it is the prior.

For the uniform-prior Bernoulli experiment with d ≥ 1, 0 < τ ≤ 1/4 and 0 ≤ n ≤ τ⁻², posterior coordinates are conditionally independent and L_j(S) = log((1+2τ)/(1−2τ))ΣY_iX_ij. For 0 < δ < 1, with probability at least 1−δ, max_j|L_j(S)| ≤ 15τ√(2n log(2d/δ)).

Assume AC. In the Gaussian-prior experiment with d ≥ 1, n ≥ 0, σ > 0 and ε ≥ 0, every jointly Borel learning rule has expected outer robust risk at least (1/2)P(√(n/(σ²+n))||V||∞ ≤ ε), where V ∼ N_d(0,I_d). Consequently, for d ≥ 2 and n ≤ ε²σ²/(8 log d), this risk is at least (1−1/d)/2.
